lines.english: "…By the way."
"Yes?"
"Where's your report for the concert yesterday?"
"About that…"
"…Or well, perhaps it's too much to expect the report of last night to be done the morning after. Fine, we'll take care of it next time."
There's no need to theorize…
What I did yesterday was a fatal mistake for my job. An error that is incomparable to what happened with Setsuna.
"Yes, everything you've done so far is good. To be honest, I think you've brought out a lot of her charm as a person. You've been crossing a lot of lines, haven't you?"
"Thank you very much."
Normally I would inform my superior about yesterday's blunder and await further instructions…
I feel like more than just a failure for being worried about how I'm going to come up with an appropriate excuse during the next report.
"Now, back to what we were talking about. How was the concert? I couldn't go myself due to work."
"Ah, well, um…"
But crime just doesn't pay, so I won't be able to hide this forever.
"What's the matter? You seem perplexed. Could it be that it wasn't anything special?"
"No, it's not that… Um, I'm really sorry, the truth is…"
"Then… that means this article was right all along."
"…Article?"
"There's a short article about the concert yesterday in the culture column of this morning's Eastern Line Post… but this is…"
Unaware that I was just about to confess, Hamada-san throws the newspaper in his hand on top of the table.
"Could it be that… the ratings were bad?"
"No, they were pretty good overall. Even the sports magazines praised it, and the online reviews were good too."
"Does that mean…"
"Pretty much all of the articles are either about how profitable it was, or they're written by people who saw Touma Kazusa play for the first time. Actual music critics on the other hand…"
"Is it just this article…?"
"Even this one isn't exactly slamming her. They've written that her technique is on an international level."
The moment I heard Hamada-san say "her technique is on an international level," I got the gist of what he was trying to say…
I can sense the irony lurking in this article.
"Besides, this specific critic is famous for being harsh. We won't know how people really feel about it until we see the reviews in next month's music magazines."
I decided to skim through it a bit, but sentence after sentence catches my attention.
"Evidently unprepared."
"She carries the air of someone at the top, but her actual skill is far behind."
"She lacks the experience and energy to keep up the momentum in the second half."
"I must say that she's lacking in quite a lot of areas to carry such a long concert alone."
"It's just that he's been writing a lot of articles for Ensemble too. Even the chief editor seems to trust him a fair bit."
"I see…"
"She certainly was wonderful during the contest last year."
"However, yesterday's concert felt like she was stretching those twenty minutes of brilliance to two hours, making it feel lacking."
I'm not sure if he's trying to be considerate or trying to provoke me, but there is probably only one thing he wants to say right now.
"Sinking ship."
"The responsibility for this lies in the sponsor who decided to host this concert prematurely, in order to cash in on the fact that she is trendy in Japan… That is to say her mother, Touma Youko."
"Perhaps she shouldn't have been misled by the idea of 'selling her daughter at the right time,' and instead taken her time to train her."
"I sincerely wish that this doesn't affect her reputation, and that she doesn't become known as not a 'trendy singer,' but a 'trendy pianist.'"
She has the technique, but not enough energy…? He's saying that about the person who practices ten hours a day with ease?
Or does it mean that playing a concert requires a hundred times more willpower than practice?
"The chief editor hasn't said anything yet, but I'm willing to bet there'll be a change in attitude in the next special edition magazine."
She has a lot of technique, but not enough expression…?
"Technique is not important at all. What really matters is emotion and vigor. That's the kind of music I like."
The only review of Kazusa I know… is almost in complete contradiction to what Youko-san said five years ago.
Does this mean that during these past five years, she has polished up her technique… but has lost her spirit in the process?
Or…
"Can you… contact Touma Kazusa?"
"That's what I'd like to know… I've been calling them since this morning, but I can't get in touch with either mother or daughter."
"Not even Youko-san…?"
"Perhaps yesterday's concert really was a failure. Maybe they're lying low from the media."
That can't be.
For that emotional and vigorous girl to…
As if there exists a professional willful and fickle enough to become unable to properly operate her own piano because of something so minor…
"Kazusa, Kazusa."
I already knew. She wasn't in her apartment.
When I asked the neighbors, it appears she never came to pick up her luggage. Her room is probably the same as always.
…But that doesn't mean I can conclude that she decided to disappear on impulse.
An associate might appear tomorrow. She might have been staying at a hotel all this time.
She might not even be worried about the results of the concert.
I might… just be overthinking it.
Should I look for her? Me? Should I in all seriousness find Kazusa?
No…
Of course, I must find her.
Because… I promised Setsuna I would.
"My name is Kitahara from the editing department at Kaiousha. I'm always obliged. Yes, that's right, I'm the one in charge of Touma Kazusa…"
I promised to not run away anymore. I promised that I'd face Kazusa.
"I think Hamada from our company tried to contact her this morning too…"
I promised to apologize for not being able to come.
"I see, not yet… Then what about Youko-san… President Touma?"
I promised to ease Kazusa's mind.
"Then if you do get in touch, please tell them to call Kitahara immediately. I'll tell you my phone number…"
I promised to make everyone happy.
Because I'm worried… Because we're "friends."
"My name is Kitahara from the editing department at Kaiousha. I'm always obliged. Yes, that's right, I'm the one in charge of Touma Kazusa…"
And… there's nothing to worry about anymore.
"I think Hamada from our company tried to contact her this morning too…"
After all, I confirmed my feelings with Setsuna. I even made a promise about our future…
"I see, not yet… Then what about Youko-san… President Touma?"
That's why Setsuna wouldn't mind me simply being worried about the whereabouts of my friend.
"Then if you do get in touch, please tell them to call Kitahara immediately. I'll tell you my phone number…"
I'm… only doing the natural thing as a fellow human being.
"…I see. Yes, that's fine. Thank you very much. Goodbye."
"Oops…"
As I'm speaking on the phone, I lower the heat on the stew that had started boiling at some point.
When I open the lid, a pleasant spicy fragrance fills the air.
"Next is… Uwah!"
I called everyone in my line of business that I knew, but in the end, it was all pointless.
Though that's about what I expected…
There is no way the young pianist who earned the title "enemy of the media" in just a few days would ever carelessly leave any traces of herself.
…I guarded her until the day of the concert myself, after all.
"My name is Kitahara from the editing department of Kaiousha. I'm always obliged. Excuse me, but is there an Itakura from Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine…?"
And in the end, it has backfired on me right now. It seems that finding out Kazusa's whereabouts from the mass media is going to be a difficult task.
Perhaps I have no choice but to find Youko-san tomorrow after all.
That's probably my only choice, and the most safe and certain method.
"A business trip…? I understand, that's fine. I'll call back tomorrow, so please let her know that I called. Goodbye…"
"Haah…"
Either way, I should give up on recklessly looking for her outside.
I should stay in this room, with the mindset that she can return at any time.
Because there is no real reason to be worried.
If she truly has decided to disappear, it's probably just because she's sulking a bit.
If I talk to her, if I apologize to her… the misunderstanding will be resolved. We can reconcile as "friends." We can reach an agreement as "business partners."
That's why I'm just slightly worried about my "friend," and I need to back up my "business partner."
"Alright, it's about time…"
I decided to go with curry for dinner today, one that can be eaten immediately. I made so much of it that for a single person to eat all of it, it'd take more than a week.
But there is no deep meaning behind that… is there?
At that moment…
As I'm speaking of the devil, I hear a sound coming from the door of the other apartment.
"Kazusa, hey, Kazusa! Where the hell have you been up until now!?"
Look, there was no deep meaning behind it after all. I always knew she'd come back if I waited.
But my mind won't be put at ease until I give her a piece of my mind.
After all, she decided to disappear for the whole day, causing countless people trouble.
"Open up! You're back, aren't you!? I told you that I want to talk to you, didn't I!?"
As my neighbor, my friend, and my business partner, it's only natural that she gets lectured…
"…I'm sorry for the racket. I truly am sorry!"
…It was the resident of the apartment two doors away. Seeing myself in such a cliched situation gave me vertigo.
"Yes, yes… then if anything happens call my cell phone. I'm sorry for the trouble. Goodbye."
"Haah…"
"I'm back… huh? It's been a while, Kitahara-kun!"
"…We've been talking every day over email. I finished the task you gave me last night, so make sure to double check it later."
Recently, Suzuki-san has rid herself of all reluctance in the way she hands out tasks. She's truly become a professional.
But still, in my unreasonableness ranking, she still only places third after Hamada-san and one other person.
"So, why are you here at work? Aren't you supposed to be glued to Touma Kazusa right now?"
"They say she ran away… She apparently got involved in some blind romantic affair."
"Huuh!? You mean someone took advantage of their position as her ex-boyfriend and made her do this and that!?"
"Don't make up random stories. If being in the same class as someone means that you're dating them, I'd be called Iizuka Takeya by now."
"…Who's that?"
Did my expression look normal just now…? Did my voice sound superficial…?
"It's just that I've been unable to get in touch with her… for a mere two days."
In the end I couldn't find out Kazusa's whereabouts yesterday.

I contacted everyone who might have had a clue in vain, and everything I thought was a hint led to nothing. There was no sign of anyone around the time the last train left Minami-Suetsugu Station either.
In my room devoid of any color or sound, I waited for Kazusa until dawn. I started moving once the sun started to shine through the window.
I didn't get a wink of sleep last night, but my mind is unnaturally awake.
"Two days… Isn't that a big deal!? Does that mean no one knows where she's been since the concert ended?"
"We can't reach the office she's affiliated with, right? Perhaps we should file a missing persons report to the police after all…"
"If you file a report to the police and the mass media gets a whiff of it, then what will you do? That would be the absolute worst."
"No, well, that's true, but I can't say I'm content with that answer either…"

"She's obviously just doing this on a whim. Now that the concert is over, she's probably off on some aimless vacation by herself. That girl's never stopped to think about the trouble she causes others."
"That girl…?"
"That individual!"
Putting it that way is nothing but an insincere act, but…
By reassuring myself with it, I manage to just barely retain my sanity.
Because I don't want to acknowledge my own responsibility.
To admit that what I did was a fatal mistake. To admit that it had a powerful impact on Kazusa's performance…
That can't be. She is not such a weak-willed person.
She is a genius, inconsiderate and self-centered…
She's not the type of normal girl that would be influenced so easily by an average guy like me.
…That's what I wanted to believe, at least.
…Seriously, what is that idiot doing? She's always been inconsiderate of others.
"I'm always much obliged. My name is Kitahara from Touma Youko Office."
"…Kitahara from where?"
"People get stingy about personal information when they're talking to the media. Maybe he thinks their tongues will loosen if he claims to be affiliated with her…"
"He has a lot of pride about his work, doesn't he? He's turned into a splendid hyena right before our eyes…"
"Yes, yes… is that so!? At the backdoor of the concert hall at that time?"
Ignoring the concern from the seniors holding second and third place of my unreasonableness ranking, I strengthen my grip on my cell phone.
It was a callback from one of the taxi companies I made numerous calls to first thing in the morning.
"And the driver… yes, Muraoka-san… He'll be back at 1 PM? I understand, I'll be there right away!"
Late at night the day before yesterday… there was a taxi that picked up a woman with long black hair near the backdoor of Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.
"Thank you very much! Yes, goodbye."
"I'm heading out! I'm done for today!"
"Oh, okay… Good job."
"Good luck… ex-boyfriend-kun."
Yet another long battle has begun today.
But unlike yesterday, this time I won't be stuck in a cycle of wasted effort.
However, what awaits me once the problem before me is solved… is something I decide not to think about right now.
"I told you I'm not her ex-boyfriend."
"…Haah."
…However, I only felt free from that cycle of wasted effort for only a few hours.
In the end, the moment I thought I'd finally gotten a hold of a thread of hope, it ended up snapping easily in my hands.
The day before yesterday, there was indeed a woman similar to Touma Kazusa riding a taxi, and she was indeed dropped off at the Onjuku Imperial Hotel where Kazusa was supposed to be staying.
However, there was no trace of Kazusa at the hotel, and I couldn't find anyone in the neighborhood who had seen someone that looked like her.
…It was merely the description of the woman that the taxi driver gave me that weighed heavily on my mind.
Apparently she was trying to conceal her voice as she was crying…
"Ah, am I speaking to Hamada-san? It's Kitahara."
In the end, my search returns to the starting point, without any progress.
"After that, did you happen to get any calls from Touma Youko Office…? I see. And you still don't know Youko-san's whereabouts either?"
I begin to be tormented by my fruitless effort, wondering where in the world Kazusa and Youko-san went.
It's starting to get dark. The cold winter night is approaching.
Please, at least be somewhere warm, Kazusa…
After losing the few leads I had, I rummaged through my memories.
All the places where both now and in the past… I recall Kazusa being at.
First I went to Houjou High before closing, checked the classrooms, gymnasium, and Music Room 2. …She had been to those places both a few days ago and many years ago, but she was nowhere to be found.
After that, I checked Suetsugu-chou, Iwazu-chou and Shibata-san's house. …I chose my words carefully when asking the two elders so they wouldn't realize.
Just in case, I went back to Minami-Suetsugu to the apartment next to mine to see if she had returned. I'm not sure if it's a good thing or not that the moving company hadn't been there yet.
And here… is the final fortress… 6-2-12, Iwazu-chou.
"Am I… an idiot?"
I feel dizzy from the overwhelming realization.
"I'll never come back here again."
Dizzy from the idiocy that made me neglect to search for her here, because I believed what she told me.
"Is she… an idiot?"
Left for years without any maintenance, the fences are covered in ivy.
A single section has been scraped off, and it clearly happened recently.
…There are three spots where ivy has been grazed by having a shoe rub against it.
"Here we… go."
I put my hands on the top of the fence, and put my foot on the scraped off part.
I knew it, the height of this spot makes it a perfect foothold.
Like that, I raise my body to the top of the fence, and nervously jump down to the other side.
…This goes without saying, I'm intruding on private property. If my company found out about this, I'd certainly be punished.
But right now, I don't have time to worry about breaking the rules.
And then, my reasoning was proven right in a way I never wanted it to be.
When I crossed the overgrown garden, and reached the window facing the living room…
I was met with something that I knew was out of place even with nothing but the moonlight to illuminate.
Broken glass. An unlocked window. Fragments of glass scattered around.
That alone is absurdly thoughtless, impulsive and foolish enough, but there is another idiotic trace of her that outdoes even those things.
"Kazusa! Kazusa, where are you!?"
On the broken glass are stains of red…
I pressed against the window with all my might, but as if to signify the amount of years it has been left abandoned, it wasn't easy to open.
The first thing I feel on my skin when I enter is a piercing chill that might even be colder than the outside air.
Once, the pleasant Touma residence had been bathed in the sunlight from the windows. Now those are blocked by the overgrown vegetation. Add winter to that, and the temperature gradually decreases.
Forget calling this a "warm place," this is a place cold enough to kill you.
"Kazusa! Answer me! You're here, aren't you? You're here, right!?"
I don't even think about the possibility that someone other than Kazusa might be here, nor do I have any need to.
No one else would try to get inside this hollow, empty house so hard that they'd hurt themselves.
The traces of blood I found on the window continued on the floor this time. They seemed to go from the living room down the hallway.
Not even the moonlight reached that place, so I had no choice but to follow those red stains using the light of my cell phone.
Unlike my restless heart, my feet only moved very slowly.
The unreliable light from my cell phone caused me to lose sight of those red traces, so I had to crawl on the floor and proceed cautiously.
The floor didn't feel that dusty. Perhaps the real estate agent has been cleaning it regularly.
And when I reached the less labyrinth-like hallway, I was guided to my destination slowly but surely.
…In a way, it was as I had expected; it led me to the stairs going down to the studio in the basement.
Darkness completely blocked my vision, and I could no longer tell which direction I was facing. I couldn't even tell if I was moving forward anymore.
By relying on just the memories of the few times I was here, I reached out for the wall to find my way to the door of the studio.
And then… I finally reached my destination.
The place where she… the idiot known as Touma Kazusa is waiting.
"Kazusa…?"
It's the basement, which hasn't had any electrical supply for a long time…
Since there is nothing to heat the room with, being here gives me the cold, scary, and lonely sensation of being locked inside a fridge.
"Kazusa… Kazusa!"
Since I can't illuminate the whole of this vast room with such a faint light, I call out to her in the hope of a response.
"You can hear me, can't you!? That's enough already! Stop sulking already and…!?"
Unlike the other rooms, this pitch black room doesn't seem to be empty. I trip on either a cord or the broken remains of some instrument.
Finding a person under these circumstances is near impossible, but I encourage myself with the fact that the space is limited. I once again crawl on the floor, nearly tripping countless times.
And then…
"Kazusa…?"
I've finally reached my real and true destination.
The biggest idiot in the world, sleeping while leaning against the wall with her arms around her knees…
"Kazusa… Hey!"
From the same height as my hands are, I hear Kazusa's breathing.
Kazusa doesn't answer my call, but she is close to me in this darkness…
"Kazusa, Kazusa! Hey, get it together, hey!"
"…Ah! Haaa… aaah…"
Her body and breath are warm. I can tell that much by just moving a bit closer to her.
"…Aah, haah… haah…!"
Now the piercing cold room from earlier actually feels nice.
I carried Kazusa on my back and left the studio, climbed the steep stairs and made it back to the living room through the labyrinth-like hallways.
Then I gently put Kazusa down. Just like in the basement, I leaned her against a wall.
"…Kazusa?"
Her eyes still won't open. Her consciousness won't come back.
Her temperature is higher than I thought when I carried her, which makes me even more restless.
How many times has it been already…?
Once five years ago, when she had multiple sleepless nights in order to ensure our success in the school festival.
Once a few days ago, when she couldn't find her way back home, shivering in the cold rain pouring down on the city.
She's so unfair with the way she always, always tries to act tough but collapses in the end, and I just can't bear that side of her…
"Kazusa…"
"…Ah, aah, haah…"
When I get on my knees and touch her forehead, I feel sticky sweat along with her heat.
The breaths coming from her slightly opened mouth are as dangerously faint as ever.
And, and…
The thing that tears at my heart more than anything, is the blackish red coloring the back of her hand.
That part was cut deeply by glass, so even though its surroundings have dried and become black, there is still red liquid spilling out of it.
She probably broke the glass with a stone in her hand, decisively wounding the right hand that has led her to fame…
What she has done can't be described as anything other than unbelievably idiotic, unthinkable coming from someone in her trade.
"You absolute… moron…! What were you thinking…!?"
A drop of liquid resembling sweat falls on her red hand.
A single utterly idiotic teardrop attempted to laugh at her ridiculous recklessness, only to fail.
Those feeble, slender fingers in my hands move a tiny bit from that slight stimulus.
A normal woman's fingers could be described as "white and delicate," but…
Kazusa's fingers have that same whiteness and slenderness, yet at the same time I can feel an overwhelming strength, stiffness and flexibility.
"What were you… thinking!?"
Those delicate yet powerful works of art are now brutally wounded and stained in red.
It's far too unreasonable, far too sad, and far too frustrating to see this.
And it's just utterly outrageous…
"Mh…"
Before I know it, I taste something metallic in my mouth.
"Nn, nnh…"
At first, I was just trying to wipe the tears that fell on her.
I was just trying to disinfect her wound. I was just trying to make sure there aren't any glass fragments remaining.
"Chu… mh, nhm…"
I'm being far too selfish for this to be me wiping away my guilty conscience. I'm being far too rough for this to be me trying to reassure her.
And I lack the resolution for this to be me trying to convey a stronger feeling.
"Mhm… nh, chu… mh…"
But this still crosses the line I drew myself.
I'm wavering again.
This isn't just me being worried about Kazusa. There is a different feeling I have as I commit this act.
I have to scold her, I have to lecture her… and I have to apologize to her.
But none of those things apply to what I am doing right now. They have nothing to do with my kiss against Kazusa's wound, and Kazusa herself.
"Mmh… mh… ahm…"
"Ah…"
Spurred by the sensation of warmth, ticklishness, or pain…
Kazusa's right hand finally starts to properly move as I lick it.
Her arms are still weak, but the strength is returning to them. And her downturned head gradually turns up.
Her closed eyes slowly open, and the moonlight reflects in her eyes.
"Kazusa…?"
"…Haruki?"
"Kazusa… Kazusa!"
"Ah… aah…"
Amidst the darkness, she blinks three times, and then she slowly focuses on the face she should be sick of seeing by now…
Mine…
"I'm so glad, Kazu…!?"
At that moment…
She forcibly pulls away her right hand from mine, and then swings it with an exaggerated motion.
I feel an impact greater than expected on my left cheek, knocking me off balance and forcing me to put my hands on the floor.
"Wha…?"
"Uwaaaah! Ah, aaaaaah!"
Even though her mind is in a haze, she certainly didn't mistake me for some unknown intruder.
"Haruki, Haruki! You, you…! Aaah, ah… Uaaaaaaaah!"
Those eyes look at me with an overbearing light. Her mouth screams the name of none other than me.
"Stop it, sto…! Your hand…!"
She punched me with all her strength in the cheek… with the very right hand that's supposed to be seriously wounded.
"Why, why…? How could you, damn you, Haruki, Haruki… Uaaah… Why!?"
"…I told you to sto…! Stop hitting me. Stop trying to hit me!"
As I'm lying knocked down on the floor, she gets on top of me and this time even swings her left hand at me.
"Why didn't you come!? It was my… my…!"
I'm probably being hit pretty hard, with a strength that one wouldn't expect from a woman's fist.
But right now, I can't afford to feel that pain…
"I told you to stop! Do you have any idea how much your fingers are worth!?"
"Like I care!"
"…You think saying that will make everything okay!? Cut it out already!"
"Let go of me… Let go of me!"
"Like hell I'll let go of you!"
After grabbing her right wrist, I managed to get a hold of her left wrist as well, robbing her hands of freedom.
…And in exchange for robbing her hands of freedom, I give up the freedom to move my own body.
"Let go of me! Let me hit you!"
"Those hands of yours aren't for hitting people!"
"Are you, are you… telling me that… when you didn't even come to listen to me play…!?"
Kazusa presses her own body against me as I'm lying face up.
Since both of our hands are occupied, we can't separate our bodies.
…Unless Kazusa tries to do something.
"I told you to come… to listen… over and over again, didn't I? You promised, didn't you!?"
"Kazusa…"
She twists her legs sticking out of her skirt around my legs.
Her breasts, pushing up against her clothes, press against my chest. They softly lose form, yet still exert pressure on me.
Her exquisite black hair flows down, softly stroking my face.
"Liar! Haruki, you… Haruki, you… Uu-uaa, uaaah…!"
And on my face…
…Are countless wet drops falling from Kazusa's eyes.
"Uaaaah… aaaah…! Uua, uua, uaaaaaaaah! Aaaaaah! Uaaaaah!"
"Kazu…sa…"
Without end…
Streaming out along with the deepest lamentations of her heart.
"Ueeeh… uaaah… ah-aaah… Uu-uah-uah, aaaaaaah!"
It's surely due to her high fever.
Her abnormal condition has caused her to become unable to control her emotions.
I'm sure that once she calms down, she'll recall this moment as something foolish, and ask herself why she ever got so angry.
"Uh, uaaaah, aaaah, huah, aaaaaaaah, uah, uah, uua! Uuuuuuuuah, haaaa…!"
There really is no reason to get this upset. There's nothing to cause her heart to get so torn up.
I'm not a man capable enough of breaking Kazusa like this…
"Uah… kh, khhh… Uu… You… You're cruel… You're so cruel… Uaah, uahh…!"
It's been ten minutes since then… yet Kazusa's wailing hasn't stopped.
My cheeks, forehead, and my entire face is wet from Kazusa's tears.
"Did you… hate me… that much…? Is it that fun, making me suffer?"
"Of course… not. Of course that's not…!"
…I can't differentiate them from my own anymore.
"I can't… bear that… I don't want to… be hated by you… I don't want to… I don't want that… uuah…!"
Even though it's such a sorrowful scene…
Since both my hands are tied, I can't even stroke Kazusa's head as she cries and shouts.
…Of course, I'm aware that if I stroked her head right now, I'd be doing something I can't undo in so many ways.
Despite that, I loosened my grip on Kazusa's wrists countless times, only to clench my teeth and strengthen my grip again every time.
"Stop it already… Doing this will only hurt you."
"I know that, I already know that! That's why I decided it would be the last time! That's why I swore to never see you again!"
What's that supposed to mean…?
"Yet, yet… even though I desperately tried to give up, you were the one who went and ruined everything!"
She's acting as if the whole world has denied her existence.
"You're the one… who turned me back into this selfish little child!"
As if everything has been destroyed. As if nothing remains for her anymore.
"It's because you keep tormenting me…!"
It's like I'm the only one in the world to her…
"Uah… ua, uuuh… S-Stop it… Stop ignoring me."
"I'm not ignoring you… How could I ever do that?"
"I'm not strong like Setsuna is… If you reject me, I won't know what to do…!"
"You were… doing fine for five whole years, weren't you? You forgot about me and did your best, didn't you?"
After five years, the world is supposed to have changed. No, Kazusa is supposed to have changed.
"Like hell I was fine! I was never able to forget…"
And after five years, Kazusa managed to reach the top.
"But you succeeded. You became a world-famous pianist, didn't you?"
High enough that her popularity couldn't be contained in just Japan. High enough for the rest of the world to want Kazusa more than Japan…
"Even that ended two days ago. The facade I desperately tried to keep up was fully exposed. And that's… it's all your fault, Haruki!"
Despite that, just like five years ago, Kazusa doesn't try to associate with the world…
She never got down from the stage at the school festival all this time.
"Why did you appear before me again? Why did you stir me up?"
When we had our reunion in Strasbourg, I wasn't the only one trying to hold back my tears.
"It was my job. Once I graduated university, I got a job at a publishing company. Even when you disappeared, I tried to do my best…"
"…Like I care about your effort. You undid everything because you keep doing unnecessary things."
"Kazusa…"
"You broke the sturdy wall… holding back the feelings I was desperately trying to repress."
That goes for when I was giving first aid to her foot, and when I was interviewing her too…
"No matter how much I said the right things, you made it so that my body and my heart weren't able to follow along at all…"
I wore an expression that I couldn't show Kazusa, and because of that, I couldn't see what expression Kazusa had.
"Why did you accept being with me?"
When Kazusa moved in next to me, I wasn't the only one with an unconcealable happiness behind my confusion.
"Why did you keep leading me on? Why did you… act like you don't hate me?"
"Because I don't hate you, obviously!"
"If you don't hate me, then don't mess with my heart! Don't get my hopes up, and don't delude me into thinking that I'll be able to reach you if only I stretch out my hand…"
Even when she was defenselessly sleeping in front of me. Even on the way back from Shibata-san's house.
Even when time stopped for a single moment in the dusk-colored Music Room 2…
"Yet, you always run away at the very end… There is no way I can endure such painful and agonizing torture, is there…?"
I was unable to see the feelings Kazusa was hiding, because I was too desperate to hide my own wavering feelings.
"Why didn't you come to listen to my piano…?"
When the curtains were raised in the concert hall…
I was the only one who ran away.
"Even though the only reason I came back was to play for you… Even though I was supposed to finally give up by showing you the last, and the absolute best performance…"
Kazusa put her soul into her performance. And yet when she was looking for me in the audience seats…
"But you didn't come, and I ended up showing the absolute worst performance. This time, I have truly lost everything."
I "wanted to pretend" that I never noticed Kazusa's all too pure and simple feelings. I disappeared from her side, and out of her line of sight.
…And I was with Setsuna.
"Let go of me… I'll destroy everything. You, me… these two hands."
"No."
She lamented, she cried, she screamed, and she grumbled…
After letting her feelings erupt for another while, Kazusa reasserts strength in her body.
Her eyes hold a resentful glint. Her hands hold weapons ready to exact revenge.
And…
"Let go of me… If you don't… I'll kiss you."
And her breath… holds her burning, ever-fervent feelings.
"Why would you… do that?"
Kazusa's sense of reason has completely collapsed.
"If you're not going to move… I'll steal you away for real, okay?"
She's laying bare just how much she hates and detests me…
Yet her words still express her longing for me, and she continues waiting for my response, no matter how long it will take.
"You'll… regret it."
"I've been regretting it for five years."
The sweet expression she's making as she appears to have given up on thinking stirs up my desires in a maddening frenzy.
"I… abandoned you, you know? I abandoned you five years ago, and two days ago. Don't you know that all I've ever done is make you cry?"
But even so… these feelings of hers are wrong. Even Kazusa herself knows that she's making an absolutely terrible mistake.
"I thought that I'd come to hate you one day…"
"I thought that I'd look back, and wonder why I was ever stupid enough to fall in love with a guy like you…"
"Someone who's unaccommodating, annoying, has bad taste, always irritates people when he's trying to be considerate… Someone who's not even popular yet has a girlfriend who's way beyond his league."
"I saw no value nor reason to continue longing for you, so I would finally get tired and see it all as ridiculous. Then I'll be able to look back at everything like a nostalgic story to laugh at…"
"That's what I dreamed of, at least…"
See…? It's wrong after all.
The ideal future you have always dreamed of is one where you hate and have forgotten me…
Reality can't possibly be different from that.
"Haruki…"
"Kazusa, you…"
"I love you."
"…! Stop it already!"
"I love you!"
"That's just what you've led yourself to believe."
"I really do love you!"
"That's just something you've learned to think. You were all by yourself back then, so…"
"I love you so much."
"You're just being delirious. Let's get out of here and rest, okay?"
"I adore you."
"I'm a traitor, aren't I? All I've done is hurt you."
"I never want to let you go…"
"You let me go for five whole years! What are you saying after all this time?"
There is no longer anything but me reflected in Kazusa's eyes.
She's close enough for our noses to touch… The same distance as that time in Music Room 2.
"Haruki…"
"…! …Uagh, uu…"
Our situations are reversed.
"I'm sorry, I'm so sorry, Kazusa…"
Kazusa's tears have dried up, but my cheeks are still wet.
"That's right, you're in the wrong… It's your fault, Haruki…"
Kazusa is no longer reflecting on her mistake.
"So make amends for it. Don't run away anymore."
She's projecting nothing but a direct and single-hearted passion to my eyes.
"What am I… What am I supposed to do?"
"It's something very simple…"
Her wet lips open, and she blows an incredibly warm breath at me.
"This moment alone is enough… All you have to do is love me for this moment alone."
But this wasn't what I expected.
I don't mean that Kazusa's breath isn't warm; rather, something even warmer has made its way to me.
Kazusa's burning feelings.
"That's… not simple at all…!"
I'll burn myself if I accept them. The flames of her passion might even end up scorching my entire body.
"It doesn't matter if you don't want to, or don't have any interest… as long as you make love to me right now."
"No… we can't, Kazusa."
If I accept Kazusa here, I won't be able to tell why I ran away in the first place.
I won't be able to know why I sought out Setsuna…
"If you dislike it that much… If you want to run away from me as far as possible…"
"Then why did you find me…?"
But the contradiction has been present since long ago.
"If you don't want it, if you have no interest, you should have just left me be."
I can no longer reason that I did it because of my job, because I was simply worried or because we're friends; after all, those feelings just aren't correct.
"Then you wouldn't be in this situation with me either."
"Do you think… I'd be capable of something like that?"
"Are you not…?"
"Of course not."
"Why?"
"Tell me, why? Why not, Haruki?"
"Because, because…"
Because the moment I found Kazusa…
"I've never once come to hate you… and I've never once lost interest in you."
A powerful feeling other than relief doubtlessly welled up inside of me.
When I stroked her cheeks, grabbed her hand and licked her wound, the feelings I held in those moments were unshakeable.
"H-Haruki…"
The pitch in Kazusa's voice conspicuously goes up.
"That's… dangerous, you know?"
Just as I thought, her excited breathing further heats up my cheeks and my feelings.
"After all, I'll be able to interpret that as… you've always loved me, and you still love me."
"Is it okay for you to be saying that…?"
"Of course it's not okay!"
That's why I'm sure that my excited breathing is also heating up Kazusa's cheeks, and her feelings…
"…But this is the only thing I can't lie about, so what choice do I have?"
"Haruki, Haruki…!"
"Don't cry."
"I'm so happy, Haruki…"
"Don't be happy about it…"
Like that, we both come close to crossing the line into a vicious cycle, where our burning feelings only burn more and more powerful.
I can't stand any more than this. I won't be able to turn back.
It would be the point of no return.
"Just now is enough. All you have to do is love me like you did five years ago…"
And in an attempt to block my escape…
"I'll give up on you truly loving me. That privilege belongs to Setsuna. …But I want you to give me your fake love."
…And without any hesitation, Kazusa says something that she can never take back.
"Only until I leave Japan… Until the end of winter is enough."
What she desires is an imitation.
Despite her claim that it would be the same as what we had five years ago, it's something completely different. She wants us to connect in body alone.
"Embrace me. Desire me. Whisper sweet words to me…"
It would be a fake love. A self-aggrandizing love. Love that would only deceive ourselves…
"Make me lose myself. …Deceive me until the very end, okay?"
It's an option that would hurt everyone equally despite the fact that she doesn't want to hurt anyone. An option that's deplorable, realistic, yet so enticing…
1. I let go of her hands.
2. I turn my face away.
"…Why?"
Kazusa's breath touches only my right cheek.
"Why can't we…?"
Because I turned to the side. Because I averted my gaze away from Kazusa.
Because I've shown Kazusa that I can't accept her.
"You said that you don't hate me, didn't you?"
"No… I said that I love you."
"You acknowledged that it's your fault, right?"
"Five years ago, last year, the day before yesterday… it was all my fault."
"Then… look at me."
"That's enough! Why not? Tell me…"
She pushed me down, pleaded for us to kiss, and sought a relationship built on a purely physical connection…
She says she desires such extreme things, and sets them up to happen. Not only that, her appearance, social standing, and attitude all point to her being an eccentric…
"Why… won't you accept me…?"
But I know the truth.
I know that she'll get cold feet and hesitate right at the very end. I know that she's so timid that it's actually adorable.
I know that so well that it makes me want to cry.
"What's the problem…? I just told you that you can choose Setsuna…! What else could you want!?"
Kazusa's eyes turn wet once again just as soon as her tears have dried up.
Her fresh teardrops fall on my right cheek, and my own tears drip from the corners of my eyes.
1. I love Setsuna.
2. I can't lie to Kazusa.
"I love Setsuna."
"I know that."
I can see Setsuna's smile when I close my eyes.
"I am in love with Setsuna."
"There is no point in saying something so obvious."
I can see her innocent, mischievous smile from five years ago. I can see her miserable smile from two years ago that showed how tired she was of waiting.
"I love Setsuna more than anyone in the world…"
"I told you that you can still love Setsuna. She can still be the one you love most…"
I can see the genuine smile she lets out in the present day that expresses the faith she has in me.
"I love Setsuna. I don't want to betray her anymore."
"This isn't betrayal. This won't count as a betrayal… No one will become unhappy because of it…"
I can see the most precious thing in the world. I can see the very thing I've desired all this time right in front of me.
"I… love Setsuna."
"I just said that I know! Stop using that word! Stop bringing up that name!"
Something… worth throwing away everything else for…
"Setsuna is… Setsuna is…"
"Shut up!"
"Setsuna is the only one for me… Setsuna is the only one I have now…!"
It's right there, behind the person who "used to be" the most precious person to me…
"Shut up, shut up, shut up! S-S-Stop it… Stop it… Uu, uaah, aaaaaah…!"
My entire body starts to tremble.
"Uuh… uah… ughu… aaaah…"
I'm not sure if I'm the one trembling or if it's just Kazusa's trembling that's being transmitted to me. Or it could very well be both.
It's not something that I need to know anymore. …I know that I've made up my mind now.
"I can't… deceive you anymore."
"Even if… that's what I want?"
"I can't say that I love you as a lie… I can't separate my heart from it."
I can't run away, or even deceive her anymore.
"This winter is all I need. If you just tell me that you love me for a little bit…"
"If I say that I love you, you'll become the most precious person in the world to me! If I make love to you, I won't ever be able to let you go!"
Back when I put the two of them side by side in my mind, when we were connected once again.
I found myself afraid of delving deeper into my feelings. Afraid of looking at the direction they were facing.
"It won't end as a lie. It won't be able to end once winter is over."
"Haruki…"
"That's why I can't do what I did five years ago. I can't make love to you knowing full well we're going to separate."
I can tell that Kazusa is gazing at me more intensely than she was earlier.
"I can't experience a love that won't hurt anyone anymore. I can only choose who I have to hurt."
Not because of her breaths or the sensation of her tears, but from a dwelling heat in my body.
"That's why I… can't accept you right now… I'm sorry."
"Does that… Does that mean…?"
"Stop talking."
"Could it, could it mean that… even if it's the tiniest hope…"
"Don't say it! That could never happen!"
"…! S-Sorry."
The reason I instinctively raised my voice is because she proposed a possibility that would be far too painful.
She proposed the possibility of a preposterous choice.
She proposed a possibility that defies common sense, one that would only serve to make even me delirious.
"No way… What was I just trying to say? How could I say something so unthinkable…?"
Even Kazusa shrinks upon realizing that she had stumbled upon that forbidden, evil option…
"That's enough, stop it. I don't want to think anymore today."
"Haruki…"
"You were just being delirious, and I just happened to lose my composure. Let's just… leave it at that…"
"…! …Uuh, kh… ah…!"
"Uuh… uah…! Uugh… aaaah…"
My entire body starts to tremble.
"Haruki… Haruki…"
I'm not sure if I'm the one trembling, or if it's just Kazusa's trembling that's being transmitted to me. Or it could very well be both.
It's not something that I want to think about anymore. I don't want to think about anything or anyone.
I don't want to make a decision yet.
"Yes, yes… Then, please do."
"The taxi… will be here in ten minutes."
"Okay…"
I let go of her hands, and she moved away.
We both sat against the wall, and then brought ourselves close to each other again.
We don't hold each other's shoulders, and we don't hold hands.
Kazusa rests her head on my shoulder, and continues her usual feverish breaths.
But I don't hold her anywhere. I don't warm Kazusa up.
"Hey, Haruki."
"Hm?"
Our screams and lamentations are over. In the darkness illuminated by the moonlight, the room returns to the usual quiet…
"If… if by any chance, I return to Japan not to play a concert, but to simply run away…"
"If by any chance, I fail even as a pianist, fall to ruin, and come back in despair…"
"Kazusa…"
"Would you pity me, and embrace me then?"
"Would you kiss me out of sympathy…?"
Kazusa's faint murmurs are sucked in by the vast room.
"That will never happen…"
"That will never happen… so it's pointless to think about it."
"…I'm sorry, Haruki."
"…I'm sorry, Kazusa."
And this time…
A true silence settled between us.
